subject: Premium support uplift discussion & pilot terms
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@hightower.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Premium support requirements & rough budget

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — the latency profile looks promising. We're kicking off an internal evaluation and need to scope premium support / SLA pricing so we can build the business case for a committed pilot. High level ask:

- Target SLA: 99.95% (global) with regional failover
- P1 response: 1 hour; P2: 4 hours; P3: 24 hours
- 24/7 on-call escalation for P1/P2 during pilot (1 named escalation contact)
- Committed monthly throughput: ~1M tokens/month initially, with growth to ~3M in 6 months

Can you share a pricing grid and examples of what a Boeing-of-support retainer looks like? Any upfront discounts tied to commitments would be helpful — procurement has a 30% baseline expectation for year-one discounts for new vendors.

I've attached a short SOW and our procurement contact is looped (procurement@hightower.ai). Happy to schedule 30 minutes next week to align.

Thanks,
Elaine
Head of Platform Partnerships
Hightower Analytics

Attachment: Hightower-SOW.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@hightower.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium support requirements & rough budget

Hi Elaine —

Appreciate the clear requirements and the SOW. Looping in Kimberly (Enterprise Ops pricing) and Naomi (Customer Success) so we can give a concrete proposal. Quick summary of what we can offer and a pilot-friendly path: 

1) Price tiers (monthly retainer + credits model)
   - Standard: 99.9% SLA, business-hours triage, P1 4h, P2 12h — retainer = 7.5% of committed monthly spend (est: $2k/mo at your initial volumes)
   - Enhanced: 99.95% SLA, 24/7 triage for P1, named escalation, P1 2h, P2 6h — retainer = 12% of committed monthly spend (est: $4k/mo)
   - Premium: 99.99% SLA, 24/7 on-call + dedicated war room for critical incidents, P1 1h, P2 4h — retainer = 18% of committed monthly spend or flat $6k/mo (whichever is higher)

Notes on credits & credits consumption:
- Each P1 incident consumes a block of "war-room" credits; we price excessive P1s on an overage basis.
- We include a baseline of 6 incident credits per year in Premium and 3 in Enhanced. Additional packs available.

2) Discounting & first-year uplift
   - For a 12-month committed pilot at 1M tokens/mo we can offer a 20% first-year discount on retainer + waived setup fee.
   - If you commit to 3M tokens/mo (annualized) we can consider a 25–30% discount tier; requires expanded committed capacity (Dedicated) and a short implementation SLA.

3) Regional failover & availability
   - Regional failover is included as an optional add-on for Enhanced and Premium. If you need guaranteed cross-region pop-ups with warm standby, that is priced as an availability uplift (additional 4–6% of committed spend).

I'm attaching our price grid so you can see the math. If procurement is asking for 30% baseline, let's treat that as a negotiating anchor and work toward a 20–25% outcome depending on commitment.

Proposed next steps: 30-min alignment with procurement + ops (I can do Thurs 11–12 PT). If that works, I'll send a one-page pilot addendum and a short-term retainer invoice for the first month.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-Premium-Price-Grid.pdf (pdf, 128KB)

Quick internal follow-up before we lock terms with Hightower: a few clarifying items we should be explicit about in the pilot addendum so procurement doesn't push back later.

- Credit burn mechanics: define what constitutes a P1 (customer-facing outage with degraded availability > 5 minutes?) and how credits are replenished. Recommend we include an incident review within 7 days to validate credit consumption.
- War-room vs on-call: war-room credit should cover an engineer + manager for the first 8 hours; overages billed hourly.
- Regional failover SLA: if they want warm standby in a second region we should track the cost as an availability uplift, not part of baseline Premium.
- Prorates and true-ups: call out monthly true-up based on token consumption; retainer covers up to committed tier, overage tokens billed at list with a 60-day lookback true-up.

One more thought — we could offer a "flex-retainer" for the pilot: lower flat retainer ($2k) + discounted incident packs (e.g., 6 P1 packs at 35% off) to reduce procurement friction. If the pilot hits the volumetric milestones, we auto-convert to Enhanced at the agreed discount.

If you want, I can draft the short addendum language (I have a template).

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Ops
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Kim —

Thanks for the rapid follow-up and the price grid. Procurement pushed back on the 18% retainer for Premium — their target is a 30% discount on services for year one if we commit to 1M tokens/mo. Proposed counter from our side: 1) 3-month pilot at 1M tokens/mo, 2) Premium-level support during pilot but with a capped retainer of $3,500/mo, 3) if we convert to 12-month contract at >=1M tokens/mo they will move to 25% discount in year one and the retainer moves to the standard percentage.

We'd like to avoid long legal negotiations — can Redwood do: 3-month pilot, $3,500/mo flat retainer (Premium features), waived setup, and a 20% discount on retainer if we convert to annual at 1M tokens/mo? If you can add one named escalation engineer during the pilot that would be ideal.

Let me know — procurement is trying to finalize vendors this month.

Best,
Elaine
